title: Geometrical Optics
standard_text: Refraction and the refractive index, n = c/v; Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; the critical angle and total internal reflection; uses of total internal reflection such as optical fibres and endoscopes. (summary of the senior secondary Physics curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Physics worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): refraction, the index of refraction, refraction and total internal reflection, total internal reflection and snell's law problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
key_sub: Light bends towards the normal when it slows down.
body_html:
How to think about it

Refraction is the change in direction of light as it passes from one medium to another, because its speed changes. The refractive index of a medium is n = c/v; a larger n means light travels more slowly. Angles are measured from the normal.

When light goes from a denser to a less dense medium, it bends away from the normal. At the critical angle the refracted angle is 90°; for larger angles all the light is reflected back (total internal reflection). This is used in optical fibres for telecommunications and endoscopes in medicine.

Example

Light slows from 3 × 10⁸ to 2 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹ in glass. n?

n = c/v

Answer: 1.5

Example

When can total internal reflection happen?

Think about which medium the light starts in.

Answer: when light goes from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle bigger than the critical angle

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
  • Thinking total internal reflection can happen going into glass.
  • Thinking light speeds up in water.

faq.q: Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
faq.a: Light from the straw refracts at the water surface, so it seems to come from a different place.
Diamond has a very high refractive index and a small critical angle, so light is totally internally reflected many times.

items.q: A ray enters crown glass (refractive index 1.52) from air and is refracted at 35° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.52 × sin 35°, so i = 60.7°.

items.q: Chioma notices: “A pencil in a glass of water looks broken at the water's surface.” What explains this?
c: Light bends as it passes from water into air.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Light passes from air into glass (refractive index 1.5) at an angle of incidence of 20°. What is the angle of refraction?
A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 60° and an angle of refraction of 41°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 60° ÷ sin 41° = 1.32.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A ray enters perspex (refractive index 1.5) from air and is refracted at 15° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.5 × sin 15°, so i = 22.8°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 45° and an angle of refraction of 28°. What is the refractive index?
